findings.rule: c1/c3 money invariant: a successful tailoring always spends one credit; concurrent starts cannot overdraw (bright line: TOCTOU on read-then-act)
findings.trigger: User with 1 credit starts job A (202, credit_reserved). Near A's completion the user posts a new requestId B. B's begin, under the user advisory lock, reads the wallet (tailoring.ts:86, free=1). finish(A) runs in database.transaction WITHOUT the user lock (tailoring.ts:150), commits SUCCEEDED and free=0. B then reads RUNNING reserved rows (tailoring.ts:93) under READ COMMITTED and sees none, so 1 - 0 >= 1 and B is accepted (202). B succeeds, spendCredit finds 0 and spendTailoringCredit returns silently (wallet.ts:168): two SUCCEEDED tailorings, one TAILORING -1 row, wallet 0/0. Each losing attempt is a free 402, so an attacker can poll A and spam starts to win the window; one free tailoring per win, repeatable per credit.
findings.title: Start racing the reserved job's finish reads a stale wallet and runs a second tailoring for free
findings.proof: Reproduced on local Postgres 16 at eea5177: a node:test copy of test/tailormyresume-spend-per-tailoring.test.ts setup plus a pg.Client.prototype.query hook that only delays A's finish UPDATE until B's wallet SELECT has returned, and delays B's credit_reserved SELECT until A is SUCCEEDED. Result: second POST 202, rows [SUCCEEDED, SUCCEEDED], ledger [[TAILORING,-1,<A id>]], wallet [0,0]; assert 402 fails. Fix: take lockUser(transaction, row.userId) at the start of finish's transaction (or SELECT the wallet FOR UPDATE in reserveCredit), and make the unreachable no-credit branch in spendTailoringCredit throw or log instead of returning silently.
